resolutions.researcher_notes: Egypt Oil & Gas feature (15 Jul 2024), citing Wood Mackenzie research, names 'Damanhur-Tanta' as one of 10 currently-existing main pipelines serving the Nile Delta/Cairo/Nile Valley area, discussed in the present tense alongside the rest of the operating national gas grid. Confirms operating status; single source, so medium/not independent.
Same article discusses Damanhur-Tanta as part of Egypt's natural gas distribution/transmission grid — it is a natural gas pipeline, not oil/NGL. Single source.

Damanhur-Tanta is listed among the 10 trunk lines (Abu Madi-Talkha, Talkha-Tanta-Cairo, Abu Madi-Damietta, etc.) that make up the Nile Delta backbone of the national gas grid — a transmission-grade interconnector, not a local distribution line. Single source, medium tier.

Article states verbatim: 'The Damanhur-Tanta line has the largest natural capacity with 700.1 mmcf/d' — exact match to the sheet's 700.10 MMcf/d. Single source (citing Wood Mackenzie research it does not itself reproduce independently), so medium/not independent rather than high.

The article only gives an aggregate length (612 km total for all 10 Nile Delta trunk lines combined), not a per-line figure for Damanhur-Tanta, so it cannot support the sheet's 60.00 km value. Checked the EGAS Annual Report 2018 (full pdftotext scan) and GASCO's gas-grid page — neither names a Damanhur-Tanta line or its length. No replacement found.

The sheet's only asserted location values here are StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea = Egypt (no city/governorate cells populated). The article places the Damanhur-Tanta line squarely within Egypt's domestic Nile Delta grid, confirming the trivial country-level fact. Low tier given how thin the claim is.
